record.context_brief: Existence of the putative [72,36,16] Type II code
record.original_question: Does there exist a binary Type II self-dual code with parameters [72, 36, 16], where Type II means that the code is self-dual and every codeword weight is divisible by 4?

evidence.quote: We say that a code is self-dual if C = C⊥. ... If a binary self-dual code has all weights congruent to 0 (mod 4) then the code is said to be Type II.
Open Question 7.1. Does there exist a Type II [72, 36, 16] code?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code of length n is a linear subspace C ⊆ F_2^n. The Hamming weight of a codeword is the number of its nonzero coordinates, and the minimum distance d(C) is the minimum Hamming weight among nonzero codewords. The dual code is C^⊥ = { x ∈ F_2^n : x·c = 0 for all c ∈ C }, where x·c is the standard inner product modulo 2. A code C is self-dual if C = C^⊥, which forces dim C = n/2. A binary self-dual code is called Type II (doubly even) if the Hamming weight of every codeword is divisible by 4; this requires n ≡ 0 (mod 8). For a Type II code of length n, the minimum distance satisfies d ≤ 4⌊n/24⌋ + 4, and a code attaining this bound is called extremal.

Question: Does there exist a binary Type II self-dual code with parameters [72, 36, 16] (i.e., length 72, dimension 36, and minimum distance 16, with all codeword weights divisible by 4)?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of an extremal Type II [72,36,16] binary self-dual code, posed by Sloane in 1973, is a long-standing open problem in coding theory. Substantial partial results restrict the possible automorphism group of such a code (e.g., it cannot contain S_3, A_4, D_8, or an elementary abelian group of order 8; its order must be 5 or a divisor of 24), but as of recent surveys the existence question itself remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Automorphism Group of an Extremal [72,36,16] Code
status_evidence.snippet: Restricts possible automorphism groups of any putative extremal [72,36,16] Type II code.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is still open; only restrictions on the automorphism group are known.

status_evidence.title: The automorphism group of a self-dual [72,36,16] code is not an elementary abelian group of order 8
status_evidence.snippet: Further automorphism group restrictions for a putative [72,36,16] code.
status_evidence.claim: Researchers continue to rule out automorphism subgroups, indicating the existence problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Is there a (72,36) d=16 self-dual code? (Sloane)
status_evidence.snippet: Original 1973 question on the existence of a [72,36,16] self-dual code.
status_evidence.claim: The problem originated in 1973 and remains a celebrated open problem.
